paraphrase: The Advaitin may take part in debate on the basis of the practices accepted by both parties without committing himself to the reality of the means of knowledge; every definition the opponent offers (of valid cognition, of the categories) can be shown to fail, so that difference cannot be established.

(Śrīharṣa, answering the charge that his method is the Mādhyamika's:) the Saugata (Mādhyamika) and the Brahma-vādin agree that the world of difference cannot be determined as existent or non-existent; they differ in that the former declares everything, consciousness included, indeterminable, while the Brahma-vādins hold that the universe other than consciousness is different from both being and non-being.
notes: Recalled; exact locus in the first pariccheda to be fixed in Phase C. An Advaitin's own acknowledgement of methodological affinity with Madhyamaka together with a stated difference.
